records.hold_reason: The source diagram orders T-Q-P and T-R-S, with R nearer T than S. Power of a point gives TR=24×8/12=16 cm, but TS is only 12 cm, contradicting the drawn ordering. No circle can satisfy all printed conditions. Hold instead of publishing A while ignoring the figure.

The rendered cubic crosses the horizontal axis at −1, 0 and 1, so A is mathematically correct. However option C is printed as “x, −1” without a legible relation, and no independently legible original establishes the missing symbol. Hold the incomplete alternative; do not invent its relation. The graph itself is available and is not the blocker.

Factoring gives (x−y)(x+y)/((2x−y)(x+y))=(x−y)/(2x−y), excluding x+y=0 and 2x−y=0, matching C. But option A prints “x + − y” and option B has displaced numerator/fraction bar. These are defects in the rendered source, not merely the import. Retain hold pending legible alternatives; do not silently choose which extra sign to remove.

At 210° the exact triple is (−1/2, −√3/2, √3/3). Printed A has positive √3/2 in the cosine position; B has positive sine too; C and D differ further. No option gives the required negative cosine. Hold rather than adding the missing minus to A.

The identity sec²θ=1+tan²θ yields sec²θ=(m²+n²)²/(4m²n²). Therefore secθ has two possible signs without a quadrant restriction. Printed B is a possible positive-sign choice, but the source never specifies acute θ or signs of m,n. For the same tangent, θ and θ+180° have opposite secants. A is algebraically wrong; hold the missing sign context.

For points on the same side of the pole, h=4√3 m; for opposite sides, h=2√3 m. The prompt states collinearity but not the side arrangement. Moreover printed B is 8√3/2 m, exactly equal to C=4√3 m. There is no unique option even under the intended same-side interpretation. Hold both ambiguity and duplicate-correct alternatives.

The complete rendered prompt is “What is the circumference of radius of the earth?” It never defines R or θ, nor specifies a latitude circle. A latitude circumference could be 2πR cosθ; a great circle has circumference 2πR. Inferring latitude only from the options would invent the missing question, so hold.

The rendered text says square side 8 cm and lateral edge 4.3 cm. The centre-to-corner distance is 4√2 cm, already greater than 4.3 cm. Thus h²=4.3²−32=−13.51, impossible for a real pyramid. The page shows a decimal dot, not a recoverable radical. Do not replace 4.3 with 4√3 to fit C.

It can represent dropping a perpendicular from P (B), or constructing the perpendicular bisector of QR (A), depending on which points were given and the order of compass steps. Neither the prompt nor the diagram specifies that initial construction data. Hold the non-unique construction identification.

The stated times give daylight 13 h 30 min and darkness 10 h 30 min. Every printed option instead uses degrees, with C=202°30′ and 157°30′ corresponding to Earth turning at 15°/h. The prompt does not ask for angular rotation or define such a conversion. Hold the unit mismatch rather than rewriting the task to fit C.

The printed expression has adjacent (x²+x)²(2x+2)² with no subtraction sign. As a product it factors to 4x²(x+1)^4, absent from all options. If a missing minus were assumed, it would factor to (x+1)²(x−2)(x+2), also absent: D includes an extra square on (x+2). Hold both missing operator and options rather than correcting several source elements to fit.

For x=8,y=1 the quotient is 7 whereas displayed B is 4+2+1=7 only accidentally; at x=27,y=4 the quotient is 23 whereas B is 9+3+4^(2/3), not 23. No supported cube identity repairs this source without changing exponents/options.

If the middle less-than were a misprinted minus, 1 < 5−2x < 7 instead yields −1 < x < 2 and integers 0,1, also absent. All options include incorrect endpoints or unrelated integers. Hold; do not weaken strict inequalities.
